chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from 'Ali عليه السلام, who said:
“Any place entered without permission, from which a thief steals, there is no cutting off of the hand upon him; meaning the bathhouse and the mills.”

key_terms.قَطْعَ: amputation as the hadd punishment for theft
key_terms.مَدْخَلٍ: a place of entry or accessible location

ai.seo_question: Does the hadd punishment for theft apply when something is stolen from a place open to entry without permission?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning theft from places that are generally entered without specific permission. It states that the hadd punishment of amputation does not apply in such cases, and mentions the bathhouse and mills as examples.
